Belobug's fork of VIctory for AMD Radeon, run on an all-AMD PC: Radeon RX 9070 XT 16 GB, Ryzen 7 9800X3D, 64 GB RAM, Windows 11. PortWatch has seen it running: GTA VI's open world renders lit, with textures, people, vehicles, vegetation, water and sky, and looks close to the retail game. It plays through missions at about 4 fps and rarely crashes.

DexNom Runtime, a fork of VIctory for AMD Radeon, tested on a Radeon RX 7900 XTX. It builds on ZSlayerHQ's victory-world-runtime with its own fixes for shaders, texture streaming and GPU memory. PortWatch has seen it running with ray-traced lighting working, the first AMD build on our board to get it: the open world looks close to the retail game, and it plays through missions at about 3-4 fps (about 1 fps with ray tracing on), rarely crashing.
Ray-traced lighting working, seen by PortWatch: the first AMD build on our board to get it
Translates 25,742 of the 25,758 shaders in its test archive; all 2,191 vertex shaders pass Microsoft's DXIL validator (its report)
About 1 fps with ray-traced lighting on; 3.5-4 fps indoors in Chapter 1's city without it (its test report)
Its README still calls ray-traced lighting experimental, and its test report finds interior lighting wrong (overexposed doorways, dark objects)

A private group's build on JoshuuDev's victory-amd fork of VIctory, verified by PortWatch. It runs GTA VI with ray-traced lighting at about 3-5 fps, almost never crashes, and gets as far into the story as the leading public builds. The in-game phone renders really well, and the map menu runs at a higher frame rate. It's built mostly for AMD and also works on NVIDIA, at a lower frame rate. Code not public.
